title: A tripped session that cannot receive the hang-up and prints nothing is ended by the runner, not held forever
purpose: DIRECTORY-050 R5 ends a session at its usage limit with a hang-up and moves it to the next account. Since cd41785a the runner repeats the hang-up when the generation prints after the first one, and kills the process group REPEAT_GRACE (2 s) after that repeat if the same leader still runs. Waffles' read of cd41785a (10 Oct 2026 13:16) names the gap left: the escalation hangs off the repeat and the repeat hangs off output, so a program that cannot receive the hang-up and prints nothing after it is never repeated and never killed, and the generation's watch waits on its exit with no clock. It is real on macOS: /bin/sh is GNU bash 3.2.57, and a shell that runs `exec` from inside its SIGHUP trap hands the new program SIGHUP blocked (probe: `PROBE blocked=['SIGHUP'] HUP=SIG_DFL`); a trap that execs without printing leaves a silent program the runner can only wait on. The only ends today are by hand: an operator stop with kill, or a second stop (session/stop.rs). Waffles ruled the number at 13:18: the first hang-up gets FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE, 10 s, because the grace after a clean hang-up exists so the program can finish writing its session file, which is user data, and this Mac sat at load 59 on 10 Oct; REPEAT_GRACE stays 2 s after the repeat, because a program that printed after the hang-up has shown it is still running, not exiting.
task: In lys-runner, give each tripped generation one escalation armed at its first hang-up: a one-shot thread whose deadline is FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE (10 s) after the first hang-up, brought forward to REPEAT_GRACE (2 s) after the repeat hang-up when the program prints and is told again. At the deadline, if the same leader (pid and start time) still runs, it kills the process group with SIGKILL and says which grace expired and its seconds. Name both graces as constants with their reasons, pin each with its own test, prove the silent case with a runner test whose program blocks the hang-up and prints nothing, and keep every existing rotation test passing.

requirements.title: The escalation is armed from the first hang-up, with a grace for each hang-up
requirements.spec: Behavioural. THE SYSTEM SHALL, when a generation's output trips its usage limit and the runner sends its first hang-up (pty::end returns Ok), arm one escalation for that generation: a thread of its own whose deadline is FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE after the first hang-up. FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE is a named constant of 10 s in session/lifecycle/terminal.rs, and its doc line gives the reason (Waffles 10 Oct 2026 13:18): the grace after a clean hang-up lets the program finish writing its session file, which is user data, and a 2 s window is not safe on a loaded machine (load 59 on Tom's Mac that day). When the program prints after the first hang-up and the runner repeats it, the same escalation's deadline is brought forward to REPEAT_GRACE (2 s, unchanged) after the repeat, if that is sooner; REPEAT_GRACE's doc line gives its reason: a program that printed after the hang-up has shown it is still running, not exiting. A generation never has more than one escalation, so it is killed and stamped at most once. At the deadline the thread calls pty::kill_if_still with the leader recorded at the first hang-up, and when it answers true says on stderr, naming the grace that expired and its seconds, either `session <id>: rotation_signal_escalated: still running 10 s after the first hang-up (FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE); its process group was killed` or `session <id>: rotation_signal_escalated: still running 2 s after the repeated hang-up (REPEAT_GRACE); its process group was killed`. The reader still never waits on a clock; a leader that exited, or whose pid now names another process, is left alone.
acceptance: A unit test in session/lifecycle/terminal.rs pins FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE == Duration::from_secs(10).
A unit test in session/lifecycle/terminal.rs pins REPEAT_GRACE == Duration::from_secs(2).

A rotating session whose script is `trap 'trap - HUP; exec cat' HUP; echo "at $LYS_ACCOUNT_HANDLE: usage limit reached"; read -r line` on two accounts ends with ended.how == AccountsExhausted, ended.status == None and ended.signal.is_some(), and the test finishes in under 40 s.

The same session's stderr carries `rotation_signal_escalated: still running 10 s after the first hang-up (FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE)` exactly once per generation (twice for two accounts), no `rotation_signal_repeated` line and no line naming REPEAT_GRACE, because the program printed nothing after the hang-up.

a_program_that_drops_one_hang_up_is_told_again_when_it_prints passes, its stderr carrying exactly one `rotation_signal_escalated` per generation and that line reading `still running 2 s after the repeated hang-up (REPEAT_GRACE)`, with no line naming FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE.
A rotating session whose program exits on the first hang-up (`echo "at $LYS_ACCOUNT_HANDLE: usage limit reached"; read -r line`, no trap) ends with no `rotation_signal_escalated` line on stderr.

requirements.title: The kill reaches only the leader that was hung up
requirements.spec: Behavioural. THE SYSTEM SHALL kill only a process group whose leader is the process the hang-up was sent to, judged by pid and start time when the grace ends (pty::kill_if_still, cd41785a). A leader that exited during the grace is not signalled and nothing is said; a pid reused by another process within the grace is not signalled.
acceptance: A rotating session on two accounts whose script is `echo "at $LYS_ACCOUNT_HANDLE: usage limit reached"; read -r line` (no trap, so the shell is ended by the hang-up within FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE) ends with ended.how == AccountsExhausted and ended.signal.is_some(), and stderr carries no `rotation_signal_escalated` and no `rotation_escalation_failed` line.
pty::kill_if_still called with a Leader whose start time differs from the live process at that pid answers Ok(false) and the process at that pid is still running afterwards.

boundaries: lys-runner only. No change to the rotation contract of DIRECTORY-050 R5 (which accounts, in what order, accounts_exhausted at the list's end), to the session record, to the protocol or to any route.

Two graces, two named constants: FIRST_HANGUP_GRACE 10 s from the first hang-up and REPEAT_GRACE 2 s from the repeat (Waffles 13:18); changing either is Waffles' number, not the implementer's. A harness that needs longer than its grace to write its session file loses that file when it is killed.
The reader thread never sleeps; only the one-shot escalation thread waits.
It ships in the next Lys install; it does not get an install of its own (Waffles 13:18).
verification: cargo nextest run -p lys-runner --test runner, the new tests and every rotation test, on the Mac (Ghostty is a Developer Tool there since 10 Oct 13:17).
cargo clippy -p lys-runner --all-targets -- -D warnings, and the full Lys battery at the landing head.

Reproduce the silent case before the change on the Mac with the Python pty probe from cd41785a's commit message, the trap's echo removed, and record that the runner test hangs at the 300 s terminate-after before the change and passes after it.
